commit.message: Let developers work through findings, not just read them (0.5.0)

findings.title: A parseable but malformed last-review.json throws out of restoreLastReview and aborts startup
findings.description: The try/catch only wraps the read and JSON.parse; the display() call sits outside it. The parsed doc is cast to Finding[] with no validation beyond "non-empty array and a sha", so a report from an older format — or one where a finding lacks `file` — reaches buildTree, where `f.file.split(...)` throws a TypeError. restoreLastReview is called from startInner, whose only handler is start()'s catch, which logs "Startup failed" and sets the status bar dormant. That contradicts the method's stated intent ("a missing, truncated or older-format file just means an empty panel") and turns a stale file on disk into a window where CR-Track looks broken.
findings.suggestion: Consider wrapping the display() call so a bad report degrades to an empty panel as documented, rather than escaping into the startup path. Validating each entry has `id`, `file` and numeric `lineStart` before displaying would be a stronger version of the same guard.

findings.title: Progress pruning evicts by first-insertion order, so it can drop the commit just written
findings.description: Object.keys() returns string keys in insertion order, and assigning to an existing key does not move it to the end. Once the map holds more than 20 commits, a developer still working through an older review has their key sitting near the front — so the very entry just written by this callback can be deleted by the prune on the same call, losing the tick they just made. Rare, but it fails in exactly the case the feature exists for: a long-lived list someone returns to.
findings.suggestion: Deleting the key before re-assigning it makes insertion order match recency, which is what the prune below already assumes.

findings.title: String.fromCharCode(10) where a newline literal would read plainly
findings.description:
The separator is four String.fromCharCode(10) calls concatenated around a "---", which takes a moment to decode into "

---

". The same pattern appears at extension.ts:779 (the join in findingAsText) and tree.ts:234. Nothing here needs to avoid a literal newline escape, and the indirection hides what the copied text actually looks like.
findings.suggestion: Consider using "\n" directly in these three places — the intent is then visible at a glance.

findings.title: revealFinding still inlines the node-unwrapping that findingOf now does
findings.description: findingOf was introduced a few lines above for exactly this shape check, but revealFinding kept its own copy. Two places to change if the tree node shape ever gains a variant.
findings.suggestion: Reusing findingOf here would leave one definition of what counts as a finding node.
